Since PlantUML has no syntax for multiple triggers on one transition, the entire string becomes a single opaque event. No individual condition can trigger the transition on its own. The most natural reading of this sentence is that a single shared condition (both dist_to_front<25 AND extra_lane=true) enables a nondeterministic choice between the two targets, not that each target requires its own distinct guard. Under that reading, the model's identical guards are semantically consistent with the NL. No exact formal fact in the supplied dossier (no additional guard clause, no priority annotation, no explicit disambiguation statement) resolves between the 'shared-condition nondeterministic choice' reading and the 'distinct-guards required' reading. Therefore the candidate's guard_disjointness violation is established as a precise semantic claim, but the surviving undercutting defeater (the NL reads as permitting shared-condition nondeterminism) means two competent readings remain compatible with the same facts. issues.basis: NL segment NL12 establishes the initial-entry obligation. Source inventory transitions (25 rows) contain no initial edge for CollisionAvoidanceSystem. FCSTM transition inventory shows transition:line:71 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) as the only initial edge in that scope. Canonical IR initial_states list confirms CollisionAvoidanceSystem is absent. Working contract classifies UnspecifiedInitial as compiler_owned synthetic_state.
issues.expected: An initial pseudostate edge [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive must exist within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope, establishing collision_avoidance_deactive as the default entry state.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory for scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains only three edges: [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:71, compiler-synthetic), collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active (transition:line:72), and collision_avoidance_active -> collision_avoidance_deactive (transition:line:73). No [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive edge exists. The source PlantUML also lacks this initial edge, and the canonical IR initial_states list does not include CollisionAvoidanceSystem. The compiler generated a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state (state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:70) as a placeholder because no author-specified initial target was present.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly states the collision avoidance system is initially in collision_avoidance_deactive. The complete closed transition inventory for the CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope contains no [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive edge. The only initial edge in that scope targets a compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state. This is a definitive structural absence: the required initial entry is missing from the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL describes the collision avoidance system's internal initial state; one could argue the source intentionally omits the explicit [*] edge because the state is the first declared child and UML implies default entry to the first state. However, the FCSTM compiler does not follow this convention—it generates a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial instead—so the required initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive is not realized in the closed model.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem lacks required initial entry to collision_avoidance_deactive

issues.basis: NL1 segment; FCSTM transition:line:75 with triggers=[Autonomous_mode_start]; verify_fact initial-entry:transition:line:75 status=refuted details={has_trigger:true}; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers for Autonomous_mode_start showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at root composite.
issues.expected: An unconditional initial pseudostate edge from the model root to AutonomousMode, allowing the system to begin in AutonomousMode without external stimulation.
issues.observed: The initial edge [*] -> AutonomousMode (transition:line:75) carries trigger Autonomous_mode_start, making it conditional. The verify fact refutes initial-entry:transition:line:75 (has_trigger=true). The event Autonomous_mode_start has no reachable consumers other than this initial edge itself. The system cannot autonomously enter AutonomousMode without an external event.
issues.reason: The NL states the system 'begins' in AutonomousMode, implying autonomous entry without external preconditions. The model requires an external event (Autonomous_mode_start) to enter AutonomousMode, and no reachable state can generate this event. The behavioral consequence is that the system is dead on arrival without external stimulation, violating the 'beginning' semantics of the NL.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The conditional initial edge may represent an intentional system startup signal that is expected to be provided by an external controller or test harness. The edge does target the correct state (AutonomousMode), and once the event is received, the system proceeds correctly.
issues.title: Root initial entry to AutonomousMode is conditional, preventing autonomous system startup

issues.basis: NL1 segment; FCSTM transition:line:63 with triggers=[Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode]; verify_fact initial-entry:transition:line:63 status=refuted details={has_trigger:true}; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers for Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at AutonomousMode composite.
issues.expected: An unconditional initial pseudostate edge from AutonomousMode to InitialState, so that entering AutonomousMode automatically places the system in InitialState.
issues.observed: The initial edge [*] -> InitialState (transition:line:63) carries trigger Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode, making it conditional. The verify fact refutes initial-entry:transition:line:63 (has_trigger=true). The event Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode has no reachable consumers other than this initial edge. After entering AutonomousMode, the system cannot autonomously reach InitialState without a second external event.
issues.reason: The NL describes a single beginning action: the system 'begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate.' The 'which' clause implies the transition to InitialState is part of the same beginning, not a separate externally-triggered step. The behavioral consequence is that even after the first external event enters AutonomousMode, the system remains stuck until a second external event fires, contradicting the NL's single-beginning semantics.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The two-step startup sequence (Autonomous_mode_start then Start_of_autonomous_driving_mode) may represent a deliberate initialization protocol where the first event activates the autonomous mode subsystem and the second event begins the driving sequence. Both events are declared at the model level.
issues.title: AutonomousMode initial entry to InitialState is conditional, requiring a second external event after root entry

issues.basis: NL12 segment; FCSTM transition:line:71 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial, no triggers); complete transition inventory showing no [*] -> collision_avoidance_deactive edge within scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem; verify_fact reachability:state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:68 status=refuted; working_contract identifying UnspecifiedInitial as compiler:synthetic_state.
issues.expected: An initial pseudostate edge from CollisionAvoidanceSystem to collision_avoidance_deactive, establishing the deactive state as the starting point of the collision avoidance subsystem.
issues.observed: The only initial edge in CollisionAvoidanceSystem is [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:71), targeting a compiler-synthetic placeholder state. No transition from [*] to collision_avoidance_deactive exists in the complete transition inventory. The state collision_avoidance_deactive is unreachable from the top-level initial entry (verify fact refuted).
issues.reason: NL12 explicitly states the system is 'initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.' The model's initial edge targets a synthetic placeholder instead. The behavioral consequence is that even if CollisionAvoidanceSystem were reachable, the system would enter an empty dead-end state (UnspecifiedInitial) rather than the operational deactive state, making all subsequent collision avoidance behavior inaccessible.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (pedestrian_detected), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The UnspecifiedInitial state is a compiler artifact representing an unspecified initial target; the author may have intended to specify the initial state but the compiler defaulted to a placeholder. The collision_avoidance_deactive state does exist and has the correct outgoing transition to collision_avoidance_active.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem initial entry targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial instead of collision_avoidance_deactive

issues.basis: NL12 segment; NL13 segment (return transition); FCSTM root transitions (only [*] -> AutonomousMode at line 75); complete inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions inventory (37 transitions, none targeting CAS from outside); verify_fact reachability:state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:67 status=refuted; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers showing zero reachable consumers for both CAS events; diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for all four CAS states.
issues.expected: A path from the model root to CollisionAvoidanceSystem exists, allowing the collision avoidance subsystem to be activated and its operational states (collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active) to be entered.
issues.observed: No transition or initial edge connects the root (or any reachable state) to CollisionAvoidanceSystem. The complete transition inventory (37 transitions) contains no edge with target CollisionAvoidanceSystem from any source outside itself. The verify fact refutes reachability of state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:67. All four CAS states (CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active, UnspecifiedInitial) are unreachable. The events pedestrian_detected_... and front_inactive_... have declared consumers (transitions:line:72, line:73) but zero reachable consumers.
issues.reason: NL12 describes the collision avoidance system with operational behavior: an initial state (deactive), transitions to active state under specific danger conditions, and a return to deactive when danger clears. The word 'initially' implies the system should be in an active, accessible state as part of the overall system. The cross-view closure shows no connectivity from any reachable state to CAS. The behavioral consequence is total: the collision avoidance feature described in NL12 and NL13 can never activate, making pedestrian detection, rear collision warning, and front collision warning permanently non-functional.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (pedestrian_detected), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionAvoidanceSystem may be intended as a concurrent, independently instantiated component that is activated by a separate mechanism not modeled in this state machine (e.g., a hardware interrupt or a separate process). The NL does not explicitly state how the collision avoidance system is connected to the main driving mode.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is unreachable from the model root, making all collision avoidance behavior permanently inaccessible

semantic_adjudication.reason: NL12 lists multiple alternative conditions: 'detecting pedestrians (pedestrian_detected), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.' The word 'or' indicates these are independent alternative triggers. The rebuttal that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' does not defeat the obligation: the NL specifies independent alternative conditions, and the model does not realize them as independent triggers.
